source: Sonnet 4.6 / 5.5 dry runs 2026-10-05/06 (scratchpad wide55 + dryrun55), body text verbatim

A-46.body:
**WHAT THE RESISTANCE TRACK ACTUALLY DOES**

Most new players chase damage and ability cooldowns when they first sit down with the Cradle. Understandable - kills feel good, abilities feel powerful. But the runs that end badly rarely end because you didn't hit hard enough. They end because you bled out before your squad could reach you, or because a Tick chewed through your Hardware in a side corridor and you had nothing left when a Runner squad walked in behind it.

The Resistance track exists to close those gaps. It improves your Self-Repair speed, Hardware, and Firewall - the stats that determine how long you stay functional when things go wrong. Each of its three named perks costs 1 Energy and unlocks at a specific breakpoint in the track.

**THE THREE PERKS, EXPLAINED**

The first perk, **Scab Factory**, unlocks at 3 total Energy in Resistance. It extends how long you bleed out when downed. This is a deceptively high-value perk in squad play. The difference between your squad getting to you and your squad watching a skull icon appear on their HUD is often measured in seconds. Scab Factory buys those seconds. On Cryo Archive, where revive windows are tight and losing a body means losing vault momentum, this perk earns its 1 Energy cost on its own.

The second perk, **TCIV Resist**, unlocks at 9 total Energy in Resistance. It reduces incoming damage from Ticks, lightning, and Heat Cascade hazards. These are environmental and enemy types that punish you for standing still and for being caught off-guard in contested spaces. On Dire Marsh and Night Marsh, hazard pressure is constant - fog, environmental threats, and heavy UESC presence all compound. TCIV Resist doesn't make you invincible to any of it, but it meaningfully reduces the chip damage that quietly kills runs you thought you had under control.

The third perk, **Field Medic**, unlocks at 14 total Energy in Resistance. It reduces the time it takes to use medical consumables. If you're running Patch Kits into contested zones or timing heals around active engagements, faster consumable use is a direct combat advantage. It also synergizes directly with the Triage shell's Shareware.Exe trait - when consumables apply faster, the shared benefits propagate to Med-Drone recipients more efficiently during a fight.

**WHO SHOULD INVEST HERE**

Every shell shares the same 120 HP, and every shell bleeds out the same way. Scab Factory is shell-agnostic in its value - it's worth 1 Energy for almost any player in any squad configuration.

Beyond that first perk, the Resistance track rewards specific playstyles. If you're running Triage, a deep Resistance investment turns your already strong sustain loop into something close to airtight - faster heals, longer bleed-out windows for your squadmates, and better survivability on maps that apply constant environmental pressure. Triage paired with Resistance investment is, in our view, the most consistent combination for squad extraction in the current meta.

Vandal players who heat up quickly during aggressive plays will also find TCIV Resist useful - Heat Cascade hazards hit hard when you're already running hot from Microjets and Power Slide chains.

Solo players should weigh this track against Endurance, which addresses heat recovery, and Recharge, which gets your tactical ability back faster. Resistance isn't the top priority for aggressive solos, but Scab Factory at 3 Energy is still a trivial investment with a real payoff - you never know when you'll be fighting downed and alone, praying for a window.

**PLANNING YOUR RESISTANCE PATH**

The Cradle is fully re-spec-able at any time with no penalty. That means you can commit 3 Energy to Resistance today for Scab Factory, try it across a dozen runs, and move those points elsewhere if the math doesn't feel right for your playstyle. There's no wasted investment.

If you want to map out a full track path - how many Energy points to hit each breakpoint and what you give up in other tracks to do it - the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle) lets you preview the whole picture before you commit.

**TAKEAWAYS**

- Put 3 Energy into Resistance as early as possible on any shell. Scab Factory is cheap and the bleed-out extension it provides saves extractions that would otherwise be losses.
- If you're running Triage in squad play, extending into Resistance toward Field Medic turns your consumable timing into a weapon - faster heals mean faster Shareware.Exe payoffs for your crew.
- On Dire Marsh and Night Marsh specifically, TCIV Resist at 9 Energy is worth the commitment - hazard chip damage on those maps is consistent enough to change how fights feel across a full session.

A-55.body:
**WHAT RESISTANCE ACTUALLY DOES**

Resistance is the Cradle track for staying alive after the first mistake. It improves Self-Repair, Hardware, and Firewall, and it carries three named perks. Each one answers a specific bad moment: going down, walking into a hazard, and trying to heal while someone is shooting at you.

The Cradle is where your stats come from in Season 2. You spend Energy, roughly one per level, across six tracks, and the investment is shared across every shell. Respec is free with no penalty, so Resistance is something to try for a few runs and drop if it doesn't suit you. The track gives no numeric values for how much Self-Repair, Hardware, or Firewall you gain, so we won't invent any. Judge it by how your runs feel.

**THE THREE PERKS, IN ORDER**

Resistance has three perks. The breakpoint is the total Energy you must have in the track, and each perk lists an Energy cost of 1.

Scab Factory unlocks at 3 total Energy in Resistance. When you are downed, you bleed out more slowly. That buys time for a revive or for a Med-Drone to arrive. It is the cheapest perk on the track, which makes it the easiest first commitment.

TCIV Resist unlocks at 8 total Energy. It reduces damage from Ticks, lightning, and Heat Cascade hazards. This is a situational perk. It pays off in runs where those hazards are part of your route, and it does nothing in a fight against another crew.

Field Medic unlocks at 14 total Energy. Medical consumables take less time to use. Healing in extraction shooters usually fails because the heal takes too long. This perk shortens that window.

**WHO SHOULD INVEST**

Because the Cradle is shared across shells, you aren't locked to a role. Still, some players will feel Resistance more.

Triage players are the obvious fit. Triage's Shareware.Exe trait passes a portion of a consumable's benefit to crew members with your Med-Drone, and the listed consumables include the Patch Kit, Mechanics Kit, and Panacea Kit. If medical items are central to your kit, faster use at 14 Energy compounds. One naming warning: Triage also has a core called Field Medic, which makes Restoration Field heal allies more quickly. That is a different thing from the Cradle perk of the same name.

Solo players, especially those on stealth shells like Thief and Assassin, can lean on Scab Factory. When you are alone and downed, a slower bleed-out gives you more time to recover without a crew.

Healing is also cheap to practise. NuCaloric's Armory offers the Patch Kit as a free daily claim, and it restores health. Claim it and use it to learn the new timing rather than hoarding it.

**HOW DEEP TO GO**

Full commitment, 14 Energy, gets you all three perks, and the cost is real because Energy is limited. Every point in Resistance is a point not spent on Recharge, Dexterity, Endurance, Support, or Strength. Those tracks have their own breakpoints, and several of them also top out at 14.

For a first pass, try 3 Energy for Scab Factory and see whether the extra downtime changes how your runs end. Extend to 8 only if you are regularly getting hurt by Ticks, lightning, or Heat Cascade hazards. Go to 14 if your build leans on healing. If you want a cheap second layer, the Urgent Care Chip gives a stacking Self-Repair speed bonus on kills or downs while you are missing health, and it pairs with a Self-Repair-focused track. Pick a chip slot for it rather than assuming it fits a particular weapon.

Use the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle) to map your Energy path and preview each breakpoint before you commit.

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**

- Resistance has three perks: Scab Factory at 3 Energy, TCIV Resist at 8, and Field Medic at 14. Start with Scab Factory, the cheapest and most broadly useful.
- Field Medic fits healing-heavy play, especially Triage. TCIV Resist is a specialist pick for hazard-heavy routes.
- Respec is free, so test the track for a few runs. Keep it only if you notice the difference.

B-46.body:
**WHAT BOMBARDIER ACTUALLY DOES**

The Bombardier core has one job, and it does it cleanly: defeat hostiles while your Search & Destroy is active and the ability's duration extends. That's the entire loop. No stacks to manage, no secondary condition to juggle — every kill you land while the missiles are flying buys you more time for those missiles to keep flying.

At 70 Credits, this is one of the cheapest Enhanced cores in the game. The entry bar is low. The payoff scales entirely with how aggressively you use your Prime ability, which is exactly the kind of relationship a core should have with its shell.

**THE DESTROYER CONTEXT**

Before going deeper, it's worth understanding what you're building around. Search & Destroy activates shoulder-mounted Missile Pods that last for 30 seconds. During that window, sustained damage to hostiles periodically releases a volley of homing missiles. Hostiles caught by missile damage are Immobilized — a strong crowd-control effect that creates kill opportunities for you and your squad.

The problem the Destroyer player faces in a normal engagement: 30 seconds sounds long until you're clearing a contested POI and the clock runs out mid-fight. Bombardier is the answer. Each hostile you drop while the Pods are active stretches that window. A committed push through a cluster of UESC forces — or a drawn-out Runner fight — becomes a sustained missile barrage rather than a single burst.

We consider Bombardier ranked-viable on Destroyer. That assessment tracks: the Immobilize effect from Search & Destroy is a genuine squad-fight tool, and anything that keeps that effect online longer is worth serious consideration in ranked.

**PLAYING AROUND THE CORE**

The core rewards aggression over passivity. You do not pop Search & Destroy and then play cover — you go into the fight. The more efficiently you clear, the longer the ability runs. Think of it less like a cooldown and more like a chain reaction you sustain through forward movement.

A few things to keep in mind:

First, UESC clusters are your best friend here. Dense enemy spawns — like the Airfield on Outpost or the enemy pressure in Cryo Archive's Control and Preservation wings — give you multiple targets to chain through. One fight with three or four eliminations can push your duration significantly.

Second, Bombardier does not replace the other tools in the Destroyer kit. Riot Barricade and the Thruster are still your engagement openers. Push behind the Barricade, land the Thruster to reposition mid-fight, and *then* let Search & Destroy and Bombardier do their extended work. The core rewards players who have already learned the shell's movement cadence.

Third, pair Bombardier with a weapon that can generate eliminations quickly at the ranges you're fighting. The Destroyer's kit is built for close-to-mid engagements, so weapons that perform well in that range band — the Impact HAR at 24 damage and 400 RPM, or the Conquest LMG at 16 damage and 540 RPM — give you the volume of fire needed to rack up kills while the timer is running.

**CRADLE INVESTMENT**

Bombardier's value is tied to how often Search & Destroy is available, which means the Recharge track in the Cradle matters. The "Head Start" perk at 4 Energy gives you a partial Tactical charge at run start. More relevant here: "Primed" at 10 Energy starts every run with partial Prime charge, meaning Search & Destroy is available faster at the beginning of each drop. If you're committing to a Bombardier-centered build, hitting the Primed breakpoint shortens the time you spend waiting to activate the loop.

You can map this path on the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle) before you commit Energy.

**SQUAD CONTEXT AND VERDICT**

We rate Destroyer S-tier in squad play, and Bombardier feeds directly into why. An extended Search & Destroy keeps Immobilize pressure on longer — your squadmates can push into Immobilized targets, your Triage partner can heal into the space you create, and your Recon teammate can Echo Pulse while enemies are locked down. The core makes a team fight feel like the Destroyer's whole job is just keeping the missiles going.

Solo play is harder. The core still works, but the value of Immobilize drops when there's no squad behind you to capitalize. Factor that in.

---

**TAKEAWAYS**

- Bombardier costs 70 Credits and extends Search & Destroy's duration on kills — commit to the fight when the Pods are active, not before.
- Invest toward "Primed" at 10 Energy in the Recharge Cradle track to cut the time between runs and your first Search & Destroy activation.
- The core is best in squad contexts where extended Immobilize pressure translates directly into teammate follow-up — pair it with a Triage or Recon for maximum return.

B-55.body:
**WHAT BOMBARDIER ACTUALLY DOES**

Bombardier is an Enhanced-rarity core for the Destroyer, and only the Destroyer can equip it. It costs 70 Credits. It modifies the Prime ability, and the effect is one sentence: defeating hostiles while your Search & Destroy is active extends its duration.

That is the whole confirmed kit, so I will not dress it up. I have no figure for how much time each kill adds, and I will not guess one. Test it in a live run and judge it by feel. What we can teach is the logic around it, and the logic is good.

**WHY IT FITS THE PRIME**

Search & Destroy activates shoulder-mounted Missile Pods for 30 seconds. While they are up, sustained damage to hostiles periodically releases a volley of high-explosive homing missiles, and anything hit by those missiles is Immobilized. The window is where the Destroyer does its work.

Most Prime-ability cores either shorten the wait for the next activation or boost the volley. Bombardier does neither. It makes the current window longer, but only if you are killing. That makes it a reward for winning the fight you started. If your fights go badly, it does very little for you.

**BUILDING AROUND THE WINDOW**

Missiles fire on sustained damage, so you want a weapon you can keep on target without long pauses. A big magazine helps. The Retaliator LMG holds 44 rounds at 600 RPM, which keeps the trigger down for a long time. The Conquest LMG holds 36 rounds at 540 RPM, and its custom Infinity Belt magazine mod adds magazine capacity and reload speed. Both are mid-range weapons, which suits a Destroyer that wants to push.

For the Cradle, the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle) lets you test these paths. Because respec is free, try them all.

- **Recharge track:** "Primed" unlocks at 10 total Energy and starts you with partial Prime charge, so your first window opens sooner. "Lethal AMP" unlocks at 14 and grants Prime energy when you eliminate a Runner. That gives you more windows, and Bombardier makes each one longer.
- **Endurance track:** "Heat Purge" unlocks at 14 total Energy and reduces your heat buildup when you eliminate hostiles. Destroyer movement generates heat through Thruster and Tactical Sprint. Killing during an extended window then helps keep you mobile.

**BOMBARDIER VS THE OTHER PRIME CORES**

The Destroyer has several cores that touch Search & Destroy. Heavy Ordnance (Enhanced) reduces the cooldown of your next Search & Destroy when you defeat hostiles with explosive damage. Bombing Run (Enhanced) makes each successive homing missile in a volley deal more damage. Missile Barrage (Deluxe) adds an extra missile to each volley. Explosive Payload (Enhanced) boosts missile damage to targets near the impact.

Think of it as a choice between uptime, frequency, and punch. Bombardier gives you uptime. Heavy Ordnance gives you frequency. Bombing Run, Missile Barrage and Explosive Payload give you punch. Bombardier suits players who already take fights in close quarters and want to stay in that window. Players who prefer short, sharp engagements may prefer Heavy Ordnance.

**WHERE IT FITS IN RANKED**

We consider Bombardier ranked-viable. Our tier list rates the Destroyer S-tier in squad ranked, because it forces Holotag kills, and B-tier in solo. The Destroyer also pairs well with Triage and Vandal. For squad play, Bombardier suits the shell's job of forcing engagements. If a fight goes your way, the pods stay up and the squad can keep pressing.

Our noted weakness for the Destroyer is that it is less useful when you play for extraction and need a squad. Bombardier does not fix that. It has no effect if you are not killing.

One note on how thin this is. Community discussion of this core is limited right now, so there is little shared testing to lean on. Treat these ideas as a starting plan and test them yourself.

**TAKEAWAYS**

- Bombardier costs 70 Credits and extends Search & Destroy when you defeat hostiles during the window. It rewards kills, not survival.
- Pair it with a high-capacity weapon such as the Retaliator LMG or Conquest LMG, and put Recharge Energy into "Primed" (10) and "Lethal AMP" (14).
- Pick Bombardier for uptime. Pick Heavy Ordnance for more frequent activations. Respec is free, so test both.

C-46.body:
**WHAT 1.1.9.1 ACTUALLY CHANGES**

Marathon Update 1.1.9.1 landed on September 15 and it is a surgical hotfix, not a balance pass. The full ingested notes contain exactly one change: a fix for an issue in the Vault where holding the Sell button on selected items while Overflow was not open would sell all items in Overflow. That is the patch. One fix, one line, done.

To be clear about the scope: this is a targeted bug correction addressing an economy-damaging UI edge case, not a weapon rebalance, shell adjustment, or Cradle change. No tier placements move as a result of 1.1.9.1.

**WHY THE VAULT BUG MATTERED**

Economy integrity is load-bearing in Marathon. Your Vault is where hard-won gear — Superior and Prestige items you extracted with — sits between runs. The bug in question could trigger mass accidental selling of Overflow contents under a specific but reachable input sequence: hold Sell on a selected item, Overflow closed. For players managing gear across multiple shells or stacking Prestige loot ahead of the October 6 Nightfall Refresh progression reset, this was a real and potentially painful data-loss scenario.

The fix arriving as its own hotfix rather than waiting for the October bundle signals that Bungie flagged it as urgent enough to ship immediately — correct call given the reset is coming and players are actively managing their Vaults right now.

OUR READ: With the October 6 economy reset confirmed, the window for this bug to do damage was short but meaningful. Players stockpiling gear ahead of the reset — trying to carry value forward or min-max their starting position post-reset — were the most exposed. Now that it's patched, the main implication is: go audit your Vault if you've been selling items and are unsure whether the bug touched your inventory.

**WHAT COMMUNITY REACTION LOOKS LIKE RIGHT NOW**

The patch just dropped and this cycle's creator signal is thin — the YouTube content present this cycle covers Bungie's broader roadmap announcements and 1v3 training discussion, not 1.1.9.1 specifically. No community reaction to this hotfix is available in our sources yet. Given the fix is a single QoL correction rather than a balance shake-up, expect reaction volume to stay low — this is a welcome but quiet patch.

**RANKED AND META IMPLICATIONS**

No balance changes means no tier movement. The current meta picture heading into the Nightfall Refresh remains intact: the BR33 Volley Rifle, BRRT SMG, Bully SMG, Longshot, and V66 Lookout hold S-tier. Thief, Triage, and Destroyer hold their S-tier shell positions — Thief as the solo ranked standard-bearer, Triage and Destroyer as the squad anchors.

The more meaningful shift on the horizon is the October 6 reset itself, confirmed to include live tuning and balance updates alongside the economy and progression reset. That is the patch to watch for tier movement. When those notes drop, we will regrade. For now, hold your current builds — nothing here changes the math on any engagement.

Check the [meta tier list](/marathon/meta) for the full current standings, and keep an eye on the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle) if you are preparing a respec for the reset window.

C-55.body:
**WHAT 1.1.9.1 ACTUALLY CHANGED**

Marathon Update 1.1.9.1 is a one-line hotfix as far as we can see. The only note we have is under General: a Vault bug where holding the Sell button on selected items, while Overflow was not open, would sell every item in Overflow. That is fixed. We only have a short excerpt of the notes, not the full list, so we are reporting what the excerpt says and nothing beyond it. It lists no weapon, shell or Cradle changes, so we have not moved any tiers this cycle. Player reaction to the patch isn't in our material yet, so we aren't characterizing it.

**WHY A QUIET PATCH STILL MATTERS**

The Vault bug is an economy bug, and that is the more useful signal. Bungie has said it will reset progression and the in-game economy on October 6 as part of the Nightfall Refresh. That update also brings a new Rewards Pass, quality-of-life work, and live tuning and balance updates. The Vault is where you stage everything you own before that reset. A hotfix to stop a mass-sell accident lands right as players start clearing, sorting and selling stock.

The same Refresh ships with "live tuning and balance updates", so the current tier list has a limited shelf life. Our placements, such as BR33 Volley Rifle, BRRT SMG, Longshot and V66 Lookout at S-tier, are held for now. They are not a promise about what survives October 6.

**OUR READ:** the reset flattens everyone's stock, so cheap, reliable kit gets more valuable while the economy rebuilds. The BRRT SMG is the clearest example: Light Rounds, 1000 RPM, a 45-round magazine and CQB range. CyberAcme's Armory lists Light Rounds at 5 Credits per x60. Weapons that run on that cheap ammo should hold up better than anything on a premium economy. Expect the post-reset lobby to open with budget SMGs and Light Rounds rifles such as the M77 Assault Rifle and Stryder M1T. The Misriah 2442 and the heavier LMGs should be slower to return.

**RANKED AND SHELL IMPLICATIONS**

Our shell grades are unchanged, and the split between solo and squad is the part worth watching. Our tier list rates Thief S-tier in solo, Destroyer and Triage S-tier in squad, and Vandal A-tier in both. Triage at D-tier solo is the clearest case of a shell whose value depends on having a crew.

**OUR READ:** a reset economy punishes the shells that depend on gear you no longer have. Vandal and Thief have kits that carry themselves, namely Amplify with Microjets, and X-Ray Visor with Grapple Device. We expect them to be the safest picks in the first week after the reset. Squad Triage and Destroyer should stay strong because their value comes from the shell kit rather than from loot.

Cradle investment is shared across shells and can be respecced freely, so use the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle) now to settle your build. Bungie has said a refactored Cradle arrives in March, so don't expect the current system to stay as it is.

**WHAT TO DO NOW**

Check your Vault before you sell anything. Use [the meta tier list](/marathon/meta) to decide which weapons to take into the final stretch before October 6. If you lean on faction gear, the [Factions](/marathon/factions) page covers what each Armory offers. This is a stable window, and the next real movement should come with the Nightfall Refresh balance pass.

BlastOff-46.body:
**WHAT BLAST OFF ACTUALLY DOES**

Most players treat knockback as damage to survive. Blast Off flips that entirely. This Deluxe Vandal-exclusive passive core changes the rules: knockback no longer deals self-damage. Instead of punishing you for getting caught in an explosion, it propels you away from the blast.

That is not just damage mitigation. It is a repositioning tool baked into the worst-case scenario. When an explosive catches you, instead of eating the health loss, you get launched. The direction matters, the timing matters, and once you understand what you are working with, you stop dreading explosions and start reading them.

At 200 Credits, the entry cost is low for a Deluxe core. We consider Blast Off ranked-viable, and the reasoning is straightforward: the Vandal already rewards aggressive, high-mobility play, and this core lowers the punishment floor for players who push into volatile situations.

**WHY THIS FITS THE VANDAL**

The Vandal's kit is built around Heat and movement. Amplify overcharges your movement abilities for 30 seconds, increasing movement speed and weapon dexterity while reducing Heat from movement. Microjets give you a second jump mid-air. Power Slide is a supercharged ground-covering burst. Disrupt Cannon pushes hostiles away.

Notice the pattern: the Vandal is constantly in motion, constantly generating Heat, constantly in positions where explosives - your own Disrupt Cannon blowback included, enemy grenades in tight corridors, environmental pressure - are a real factor.

Before Blast Off, an explosive caught mid-slide or mid-Microjet arc was a hard tax on your health pool. With Blast Off, that same force extends your movement. You were going somewhere fast; now something else is also pushing you there. The geometry changes.

This is not a beginner's trick. It requires you to think about your trajectory before a fight, not after the explosion lands. Players who already understand how to read the Vandal's movement loop - when to Amplify, when to commit a Microjet jump, when to Power Slide through a position - will extract the most from it. For newer Vandal players still learning the shell's heat rhythm, this core takes some of the edge off repositioning under fire.

**CRADLE PAIRING**

Blast Off rewards players who are already moving well. The Endurance track is your natural companion here. Investing Energy into Endurance improves Heat Capacity and Fall Resistance, and its perks address the Vandal's core tension directly.

Quick Vent, which unlocks at 3 total Energy in Endurance, starts Heat recovery more quickly after heat-generating actions - critical when Microjets, Power Slides, and Amplify are all competing for the same Heat budget. Heat Dissipation at 9 Energy accelerates how quickly generated Heat recovers. If you are running a high-mobility Vandal who is constantly in and out of explosive situations, those two perks smooth out the moments where your movement would otherwise stall.

The Dexterity track is worth a secondary look. Its Full Throttle perk, unlocking at 14 Energy, grants Cardio Kick effects at the start of every run - immediate agility off the infil drop, before you have had a chance to earn it in-match. On a Vandal playing aggressively from the first zone, that early movement edge matters.

You can plan and preview the full Energy path at the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle) before you commit a single point. Respec is always free, so there is no cost to experimenting.

**THE VERDICT**

Blast Off is a core that changes how you process risk. The Vandal already lives in the gap between too-fast and overextended. This closes that gap slightly - not by making you tougher, but by making the consequences of aggression less punishing and occasionally useful. That is a meaningful shift for any player who is already comfortable with the shell's movement and wants to push into harder situations.

**Takeaways:**

- Blast Off converts knockback into propulsion and removes its self-damage entirely - it is a repositioning tool in disguise, not just a damage-reduction passive.
- Pair it with the Endurance track in the Cradle: Quick Vent at 3 Energy and Heat Dissipation at 9 Energy keep your movement options open when explosive situations heat things up.
- At 200 Credits for a Deluxe core, the cost is low. Drop it in, run a few matches, and see if your threat assessment of explosive angles changes. It will.

BlastOff-55.body:
**WHAT BLAST OFF ACTUALLY DOES**

Blast Off is a Deluxe, Vandal-only core in the Passive slot, and it costs 200 Credits. Its entire effect fits in one sentence: knockback no longer deals self-damage, and instead propels you away from the blast.

That is a short list of facts, so this will be a short guide. I will not pad it with numbers the core does not give us. What matters is the shape of the trade. Most cores add a bonus. This one removes a penalty and swaps it for movement. Knockback stops being something you pay for and becomes something that carries you.

**WHY IT FITS THE VANDAL**

The Vandal is built around moving through a fight rather than standing in it. Microjets gives you an additional jump while airborne. Power Slide gives you a supercharged slide that is faster and covers more ground than a normal slide. Amplify overcharges your movement abilities for 30 seconds. Disrupt Cannon, the tactical, fires a projectile that deals damage and pushes hostiles away, and holding the bind for 2 seconds gives maximum overcharge with a bigger blast and more damage.

Every one of those tools is about controlling distance. Blast Off belongs in that family because it makes knockback part of your own positioning instead of a hazard to avoid. Our tier list rates the Vandal A in both solo and squad, and we consider it the best starting shell for ranked. Blast Off is a core for a player who already lives in that movement-first style.

**HOW TO FIND OUT WHERE IT APPLIES**

The core's text says knockback, and it does not list which sources count. Do not assume it covers every blast in the game. Before you take it into a ranked queue, test it in a low-stakes run. A Rook or a Sponsored Kit run is a cheap place to learn how it behaves, because the gear you risk is minimal. Watch two things: whether you still take damage from the blasts you expect to be safe, and which direction you travel afterward. The direction is the important part, because "propelled away" is only an advantage if you aim your fights so that away is where you want to be.

A practical habit follows from this. Think of the blast as a movement tool you spend, not a damage tool you suffer. Position yourself so that the way you would be pushed is toward cover or toward your exit. Do not position yourself so that it pushes you into open ground.

**BUILD CONTEXT: HEAT AND CRADLE**

Blast Off does nothing for your heat. Microjets and Power Slide both generate additional heat, and a core that encourages more movement makes that budget matter more. The Cradle covers this, and you can adjust it freely because respec costs nothing.

The Endurance track is the natural pairing. Quick Vent unlocks at 3 total Energy and starts heat recovery sooner after heat-generating actions. Heat Dissipation unlocks at 9 and makes generated heat recover faster. Heat Purge unlocks at 14 and reduces heat buildup when you eliminate hostiles. You can map the full path in the [Cradle planner](/marathon/cradle). Because respec is free, try a heavier Endurance split for a few runs and keep it only if you notice you are overheating less in fights.

**IS IT WORTH 200 CREDITS?**

We consider Blast Off ranked-viable. It is also cheap, and that lowers the cost of being wrong. I have no precedent to compare it to. Removing a self-damage penalty and replacing it with free movement is a shape I cannot match to anything else on the Vandal list, so judge it by testing rather than by reputation. If your Vandal fights tend to start with a blast and end with you repositioning, it earns its slot. If you mostly play a steady, planted style, one of the other Vandal cores will likely serve you better.

**TAKEAWAYS**

- Blast Off turns knockback from self-damage into forward-and-away movement. It is a Deluxe, Vandal-only Passive that costs 200 Credits.
- Test which blasts it affects on a low-risk run before committing it to ranked, and position so that being pushed away helps you.
- Movement-heavy Vandals run hot. Pair the core with Endurance perks such as Quick Vent at 3 Energy and Heat Dissipation at 9, and respec freely if it does not feel right.
